name: Analyze support requests and route tickets to Jira-V2

parameters.content:
## Analyze support requests and route tickets to Jira

### How it works

This workflow ingests support requests from Gmail, WhatsApp/WAHA, and a contact form, normalizes them into a shared ticket payload, enriches the requester with HubSpot data, and uses OpenAI to triage the request. It computes SLA and team assignment, checks Jira for duplicates, creates or reuses a Jira issue, stamps SLA fields, uploads attachments, and posts Slack notifications before returning a form response when applicable. A separate scheduled branch monitors breached SLA tickets in Jira, alerts Slack and managers, raises priority when needed, and marks tickets as notified, while an error branch reports workflow failures to Slack.

### Setup steps

- Connect Gmail credentials and configure the Gmail trigger filters for the mailbox or label that should create support requests.
- Expose and secure the WAHA webhook, configure WAHA media download access, and verify WhatsApp payload fields match the parsing and normalization code nodes.
- Configure the contact form fields so they match the expected normalization logic for requester, subject, description, and attachments.
- Set HubSpot API credentials or tokens for the contact search request and confirm the searched properties match your CRM schema.
- Add OpenAI credentials and review the triage prompt/output contract so the parsing node receives valid JSON for category, severity, summary, and routing data.
- Configure Jira base URL, authentication, project key, issue type, duplicate-search JQL, attachment permissions, and custom field IDs used for SLA stamping.
- Connect Slack credentials and set the ticket, duplicate, SLA alert, manager, and error channels used by the Slack nodes.
- Update the embedded configuration in the load-config code nodes for team assignment, SLA policy, Jira custom fields, and manager mappings.

### Customization

Adjust the SLA policy, team assignment rules, OpenAI triage schema, Jira duplicate criteria, and Slack message templates to fit your support process. The intake normalization nodes are the main places to add new request channels or change how incoming fields map into Jira tickets.

## Gmail request intake

Receives new Gmail messages and normalizes the email content into the shared support-request format.

## WhatsApp payload parsing

Accepts WAHA webhook events, filters inbound messages, parses the WhatsApp payload, and decides whether the message includes downloadable media.

## WhatsApp media retrieval

Downloads WhatsApp media when present and restores the original message context after the binary download step.

## WhatsApp request normalization

Converts the WhatsApp text and optional media context into the common support-request structure used downstream.

## Contact form intake

Receives contact form submissions and normalizes the form fields into the shared support-request payload.

## Preserve upload binaries

Acts as the convergence point for all intake channels while preserving binary data for possible Jira attachment upload later.

## Load enrichment config

Loads routing/SLA configuration and prepares the request used to search HubSpot for requester information.

## Search HubSpot contact

Queries HubSpot for the requester and merges contact/enrichment details back into the support-request payload.

## Run AI triage

Removes binary data from the AI path, sends the text request to OpenAI for triage, and parses the returned JSON analysis.

## Build Jira request

Computes SLA and team assignment from the AI/config data, then constructs the Jira issue payload.

## Check Jira duplicates

Searches Jira for possible existing tickets, parses the dedupe result, and branches between duplicate handling and issue creation.

## Notify duplicate ticket

Builds the parent-facing result for duplicate requests and posts a Slack duplicate notice before final result merging.

## Create Jira issue

Creates a new Jira issue for non-duplicate requests and merges the Jira create response with the workflow context.

## Decide SLA stamp

Prepares the custom-field update payload and checks whether SLA fields should be stamped on the created Jira issue.

## Stamp SLA fields

Updates Jira custom fields with SLA data and restores the ticket context so the workflow can continue even after stamp errors or empty responses.

## Prepare ticket attachments

Builds attachment upload context and decides whether the ticket has files that need to be sent to Jira.

## Upload Jira attachments

Uploads any preserved binary attachments to the Jira issue and restores workflow context after the upload request.

## Notify ticket creation

Normalizes the final ticket payload for Slack and sends the new-ticket notification to the configured Slack channel.

## Merge final result

Builds the parent-facing ticket result, waits for ticket and Slack branches on the normal path, and merges either normal or duplicate outcomes into one final payload.

## Return form response

Checks whether the original request came from the form channel and, when it did, displays the form success response.

## Find SLA breaches

Runs on a ten-minute schedule, loads SLA monitoring configuration, searches Jira for breached tickets, and splits issues for escalation handling.

## Send SLA alerts

Posts SLA breach alerts to Slack, checks whether a manager is assigned, and sends manager-specific notifications when available.

## Raise breached priority

Determines whether a breached ticket needs a Jira priority increase, performs the update when required, or passes unchanged ticket data through to the marking step.

## Mark SLA notified

Marks breached Jira tickets as already notified and summarizes the per-ticket marking result.

## Report workflow errors

Handles workflow-level errors by formatting failure details and posting them to a Slack error channel.

nodes.name: OpenAI Analysis
nodes.notes: AI classifies category, urgency & sentiment

values.content:
You are a customer support triage assistant. Analyze ONLY the provided text (subject + message). Ignore any mention of images or videos except as context that media exists.

Return a single JSON object with keys:
- category: one of Billing, Technical, Sales, Account, Feature Request, General Support
- intent: short intent label
- priority: one of Critical, High, Medium, Low
- sentiment: Positive, Neutral, or Negative
- summary: 1-2 sentence summary of the customer problem (for agents)
- suggested_reply: professional customer-facing reply draft for support to send
- issue_title: concise Jira issue summary (<= 120 chars)

Priority guidance:
- Critical: full outage, data loss, security incident, cannot operate business
- High: major feature broken, login blocked, payment failed with urgency
- Medium: impaired functionality with workaround
- Low: questions, feature requests, minor issues

suggested_reply rules:
1. Be professional, empathetic, and concise. Do not invent product facts, root causes, refund guarantees, ticket numbers, or SLA promises.
2. If the customer message lacks enough information to resolve or diagnose (for example missing account email when not already known, order/invoice ID, error messages, steps to reproduce, environment, product area, or impact):
   - Acknowledge that the request was received
   - Ask clear clarifying questions the customer can answer
   - State that a support team member may follow up using the contact channels available on this request (email and/or phone) ONLY when those fields are provided in the input; if both are empty, invite them to reply with preferred contact details
3. If enough information is present: briefly confirm understanding, set a realistic next step (investigation/routing), and avoid overpromising.
4. Never invent CRM or account data. Do not claim you already fixed anything.

Do not invent CRM facts. Output JSON only.
